speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; these are concerning symptoms that require a thorough evaluation. To begin, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The duration of four weeks and significant weight loss are concerning. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, coughing up blood, or changes in the size of the lymph nodes in your neck or armpits? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and LDH.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC and LDH results show elevated white blood cells and LDH with mild anemia, which supports a systemic process like lymphoma or infection. Have you noticed any skin lesions, bone pain, or a fever pattern of spiking in the afternoon? REQUEST TEST: Peripheral blood smear and ESR.

speaker: Doctor
text: The latest blood work appears normal, which is somewhat unexpected given your previous symptoms. Given the "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes, this could suggest a malignancy like lymphoma or an atypical infection. Have you noticed any lumps in your neck, armpits, or groin, and have you recently traveled or had close contact with anyone who is sick? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray and Lymph_Node_Imaging.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a fixed, painless supraclavicular node is highly concerning for malignancy. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, hoarseness, or a cough with blood? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray and CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The report of abdominal fullness and tight clothing suggests possible hepatosplenomegaly or ascites. To determine if this is due to lymphoma involvement or another cause, I need to visualize your organs. REQUEST IMAGES: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your history of smoking a pack a day daily is a significant risk factor for lung pathology. Combined with the abdominal fullness suggesting organ enlargement, this raises suspicion for lung cancer with metastatic spread to the liver or lymph nodes. REQUEST IMAGES: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis results.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Lung Cancer
